name: effect-fence-hold-generation-unconfirmed-content-hash-mismatch
description: THE CONTENT-HASH CONVENTION, tested as a difference in the verdict. The workspace and the request are 01's, with ONE change: content_hash is the digest of DIFFERENT bytes ("superseded bytes\n"). The coordinator reports the caller's content differs from the content it records at version 1, which demotes the ownership generation to the unconfirmed sentinel -- the generation is the AUTHORITY comparand, and a hash mismatch means the coordinator cannot vouch that the bytes in hand ARE the content at that version. So 01 fires and this holds on a digest alone. That is what makes the convention (lowercase sha-256 hex over the EXACT bytes the caller holds, no normalization) enforced rather than described: test_effect_fence_corpus.py recomputes 01's digest from its file bytes and asserts that the stripped and newline-trimmed forms produce DIFFERENT digests, so an implementation that normalized before hashing would land its callers here instead of on proceed.
